line: The heart of Abbeville Village, the pretty little high street between Clapham and Balham.

name: WC Clapham
why: A candlelit wine and charcuterie bar in the old Victorian public toilets at Clapham Common station, with the original tiles still on the walls. Small, cosy and one of London's quirkiest bars.
line: A candlelit wine and charcuterie bar in the old Victorian public toilets at Clapham Common station, with the original tiles still on the walls.
address: Clapham Common South Side, London SW4 7AA

name: Venn Street Records
why: A lively bar beside the Clapham Picturehouse: pizza, cocktails and live music or DJs seven nights a week. Busy and fun at weekends.
line: A lively bar beside the Clapham Picturehouse: pizza, cocktails and live music or DJs seven nights a week.

name: No. 32 The Old Town
why: An all-day bar and restaurant in Clapham Old Town, with a fairy-lit roof terrace that's one of the nicest spots in the area for an evening drink.
line: An all-day bar and restaurant in Clapham Old Town, with a fairy-lit roof terrace that's one of the nicest spots in the area for an evening drink.

name: Clapham Common
why: 220 acres of open green between Clapham, Balham and Battersea: three ponds, a bandstand, tennis courts and playgrounds, with pubs and cafés all round the edge. Busy with picnics and football on summer weekends.
line: 220 acres of open green between Clapham, Balham and Battersea: three ponds, a bandstand, tennis courts and playgrounds, with pubs and cafés all round the edge.

name: Chez Bruce
why: One of London's best-loved neighbourhood restaurants, overlooking Wandsworth Common and holding a Michelin star for more than 20 years. Classic French and Mediterranean cooking, a famous cheese board and very good value set lunches.
line: One of London's best-loved neighbourhood restaurants, overlooking Wandsworth Common and holding a Michelin star for more than 20 years.

name: Gazette Putney
why: A friendly French brasserie: onion soup, steak tartare, snails and a good-value set menu, plus breakfast and brunch at weekends. Relaxed, with an old Aga turned into a table.
line: A friendly French brasserie: onion soup, steak tartare, snails and a good-value set menu, plus breakfast and brunch at weekends.

name: Ruth's
why: A candlelit British restaurant a short walk from the river, with comforting classics and proper puddings. A good choice for a date night in Putney.
line: A candlelit British restaurant a short walk from the river, with comforting classics and proper puddings.

name: Chook Chook
why: Indian street food in a dining room styled like an old railway carriage: pav bhaji, Awadhi lamb chops and a chocolate samosa to finish.
line: Indian street food in a dining room styled like an old railway carriage: pav bhaji, Awadhi lamb chops and a chocolate samosa to finish.

name: The Waterfront
why: A riverside Young's pub and restaurant by Wandsworth Bridge, with a big terrace on the Thames. Wood-fired pizzas, seasonal British dishes and Sunday roasts with river views.
line: A riverside Young's pub and restaurant by Wandsworth Bridge, with a big terrace on the Thames.
address: Baltimore House, Juniper Drive, London SW18 1TZ

name: The Duke's Head
why: A grand Victorian pub on the river right by Putney Bridge, and the place to be on Boat Race day, when the crews start a few hundred yards away. Downstairs is The Rowing Club, a cocktail bar. Thanksgiving 2026: a welcome drink and three-course American-inspired dinner on Thu 26 Nov, 7pm–10pm, from £54.
line: A grand Victorian pub on the river right by Putney Bridge, and the place to be on Boat Race day, when the crews start a few hundred yards away.

name: The Half Moon
why: A Putney pub and music venue that has hosted gigs since the 1960s; the Rolling Stones and U2 are among the names who have played here. Still live music most nights, plus comedy.
line: A Putney pub and music venue that has hosted gigs since the 1960s; the Rolling Stones and U2 are among the names who have played here.

name: The Ship
why: A riverside Young's pub by Wandsworth Bridge with a big terrace and summer barbecues. Very popular for Sunday lunch, so book for a table by the river.
line: A riverside Young's pub by Wandsworth Bridge with a big terrace and summer barbecues.

name: The Cat's Back
why: An Edwardian corner pub near the river in Wandsworth, full of character, with a cosy upstairs snug and an outdoor terrace. A proper local.
line: An Edwardian corner pub near the river in Wandsworth, full of character, with a cosy upstairs snug and an outdoor terrace.

name: The Rowing Club
why: A cocktail bar hidden beneath The Duke's Head by Putney Bridge, with rowing memorabilia on the walls. A smart spot for a drink after a riverside walk.
line: A cocktail bar hidden beneath The Duke's Head by Putney Bridge, with rowing memorabilia on the walls.
address: Under The Duke's Head, 8 Lower Richmond Road, London SW15 1JN

name: Putney Pies
why: Homemade pies and pie and mash by Putney Bridge, with local ciders. Later in the week the brick-vaulted basement turns into a bar with DJs and a dancefloor.
line: Homemade pies and pie and mash by Putney Bridge, with local ciders.

name: Wandsworth Common
why: A big, peaceful common between Wandsworth, Clapham Junction and Balham, with a lake, woods, playgrounds and a café. Chez Bruce looks out over it, and Putney Heath and Wimbledon Common are a short ride away.
line: A big, peaceful common between Wandsworth, Clapham Junction and Balham, with a lake, woods, playgrounds and a café.

name: Casa Fofò
why: A tiny, relaxed Michelin-starred restaurant on a residential street between Dalston and Hackney Central. Chef Adolfo De Cecco's daily-changing tasting menu is one of the best-value Michelin meals in London. Book well ahead.
line: A tiny, relaxed Michelin-starred restaurant on a residential street between Dalston and Hackney Central.

name: Mangal 2
why: A Dalston institution since 1994, now run by the founder's sons with a modern twist: charcoal-grilled meats, mackerel with green tomato ezme and sourdough pide.
line: A Dalston institution since 1994, now run by the founder's sons with a modern twist: charcoal-grilled meats, mackerel with green tomato ezme and sourdough pide.

name: Café Cecilia
why: A bright canal-side restaurant by Broadway Market from a chef who trained at the River Café and St. John. Simple, brilliant cooking: Guinness bread, onglet with peppercorn sauce, and bread and butter pudding.
line: A bright canal-side restaurant by Broadway Market from a chef who trained at the River Café and St.

name: Bistrotheque
why: A Hackney favourite for over 20 years, in a whitewashed former warehouse off Cambridge Heath Road. French bistro cooking, a lively room and a famous weekend brunch with a pianist.
line: A Hackney favourite for over 20 years, in a whitewashed former warehouse off Cambridge Heath Road.

name: Cat & Mutton
why: A lively two-storey pub at the top of Broadway Market. Known for its Sunday roast and themed quiz nights. Perfect after the Saturday market.
line: A lively two-storey pub at the top of Broadway Market.

name: Prince George
why: A proper backstreet Victorian pub in Dalston: real ales, a great jukebox, a pool room and an open fire. A favourite with locals.
line: A proper backstreet Victorian pub in Dalston: real ales, a great jukebox, a pool room and an open fire.

name: Pub on the Park
why: Right on the edge of London Fields, with a big terrace looking over the park and DJs at weekends. Packed on sunny days.
line: Right on the edge of London Fields, with a big terrace looking over the park and DJs at weekends.

name: The Shacklewell Arms
why: A Dalston pub and gig venue with up-and-coming bands most nights, a big outdoor area and late opening at weekends.
line: A Dalston pub and gig venue with up-and-coming bands most nights, a big outdoor area and late opening at weekends.

name: Three Sheets Dalston
why: The tiny original Three Sheets, on Kingsland Road, regularly named one of the world's best bars. Simple, perfectly made cocktails in a small, relaxed room. Book ahead. Its sister bar is in Soho.
line: The tiny original Three Sheets, on Kingsland Road, regularly named one of the world's best bars.

name: Dalston Superstore
why: A Dalston landmark since 2009: café-bar by day, club by night, and one of east London's best-loved LGBTQ+ venues. Everyone's welcome, and the dancing goes on late.
line: A Dalston landmark since 2009: café-bar by day, club by night, and one of east London's best-loved LGBTQ+ venues.

name: Brilliant Corners
why: A Japanese-style listening bar: records played on a serious audiophile sound system, izakaya food like karaage and skewers, and natural wines. A different kind of night out.
line: A Japanese-style listening bar: records played on a serious audiophile sound system, izakaya food like karaage and skewers, and natural wines.

name: London Fields
why: Hackney's favourite park, between Broadway Market and Mare Street, with the heated outdoor London Fields Lido, a paddling pool, a cricket pitch and barbecue spots. The place to be on a summer weekend.
line: Hackney's favourite park, between Broadway Market and Mare Street, with the heated outdoor London Fields Lido, a paddling pool, a cricket pitch and barbecue spots.

name: The Clarence Tavern
why: A handsome corner pub on Church Street from the team behind the Anchor & Hope, with big-hearted British cooking: pies, slow-cooked lamb to share and a much-loved Sunday roast. There's a garden at the back.
line: A handsome corner pub on Church Street from the team behind the Anchor & Hope, with big-hearted British cooking: pies, slow-cooked lamb to share and a much-loved Sunday roast.
address: 102 Stoke Newington Church Street, London N16 0LA

name: Esters
why: A tiny neighbourhood café that does one of north-east London's best brunches, with creative seasonal plates and excellent coffee. Expect a queue at weekends.
line: A tiny neighbourhood café that does one of north-east London's best brunches, with creative seasonal plates and excellent coffee.

name: Escocesa
why: Spanish tapas made with Scottish seafood: Orkney scallops, octopus and the catch of the day, with good Spanish wines. Relaxed and friendly.
line: Spanish tapas made with Scottish seafood: Orkney scallops, octopus and the catch of the day, with good Spanish wines.
address: 67 Stoke Newington Church Street, London N16 0AR

name: Vicoli di Napoli
why: Proper Neapolitan pizza on Church Street, in the spot that was once London's branch of the famous L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele. Keep it simple: margherita or marinara.
line: Proper Neapolitan pizza on Church Street, in the spot that was once London's branch of the famous L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele.
address: 125 Stoke Newington Church Street, London N16 0UH

name: 19 Numara Bos Cirrik
why: A no-frills Turkish grill house on the High Street: charcoal-grilled meats, beyti wraps and lentil soup, generous and great value. Good for groups.
line: A no-frills Turkish grill house on the High Street: charcoal-grilled meats, beyti wraps and lentil soup, generous and great value.
address: 194 Stoke Newington High Street, London N16 7JD

name: The Prince
why: A friendly backstreet local with a big beer garden, craft ales and a Sunday lunch that regularly makes the best-roast lists.
line: A friendly backstreet local with a big beer garden, craft ales and a Sunday lunch that regularly makes the best-roast lists.

name: The Jolly Butchers
why: A real-ale and cider house with one of the best beer selections in the area, big arched windows and a relaxed, busy feel.
line: A real-ale and cider house with one of the best beer selections in the area, big arched windows and a relaxed, busy feel.
address: 204 Stoke Newington High Street, London N16 7HU

name: The Lady Mildmay
why: A dog-friendly corner gastropub by Newington Green: dark wood panelling, a long gin list and Mediterranean food from an open kitchen.
line: A dog-friendly corner gastropub by Newington Green: dark wood panelling, a long gin list and Mediterranean food from an open kitchen.

name: High Water
why: A relaxed, moodily lit cocktail bar where good drinks don't cost the earth, with a few seats out front on summer evenings.
line: A relaxed, moodily lit cocktail bar where good drinks don't cost the earth, with a few seats out front on summer evenings.

name: Bar Doña
why: A small, dark-red mezcal bar that hosts art shows and live music. Come for the margaritas, with tacos from Tigre.
line: A small, dark-red mezcal bar that hosts art shows and live music.
address: 92 Stoke Newington High Street, London N16 7NY

name: Fontaine's
why: An art deco cocktail bar serving forgotten classics, with cabaret and live music. Glamorous, and best for a date or a small group.
line: An art deco cocktail bar serving forgotten classics, with cabaret and live music.

name: Clissold Park
why: Stoke Newington's favourite park: a Georgian mansion with a café on the terrace, lakes, a small animal enclosure with deer and goats, and a paddling pool. Lovely on a sunny afternoon.
line: Stoke Newington's favourite park: a Georgian mansion with a café on the terrace, lakes, a small animal enclosure with deer and goats, and a paddling pool.

name: The Clove Club
why: One of London's most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants, in the old Shoreditch Town Hall on the edge of Hoxton. A modern British tasting menu, regularly listed among the world's best. One for a very special occasion.
line: One of London's most celebrated Michelin-starred restaurants, in the old Shoreditch Town Hall on the edge of Hoxton.
address: Shoreditch Town Hall, 380 Old Street, London EC1V 9LT

name: Via Emilia
why: Handmade pasta from Emilia-Romagna on Hoxton Square: tagliatelle bolognese done properly, and gnocco fritto with cured meats. Simple, generous and great value.
line: Handmade pasta from Emilia-Romagna on Hoxton Square: tagliatelle bolognese done properly, and gnocco fritto with cured meats.

name: Sông Quê
why: The best-known café on Kingsland Road's 'Pho Mile', serving big bowls of pho and Vietnamese favourites for years. Busy, quick and cheap.
line: The best-known café on Kingsland Road's 'Pho Mile', serving big bowls of pho and Vietnamese favourites for years.

name: Red Dog Saloon
why: Old-school American barbecue on Hoxton Square: pulled pork, brisket, ribs and big sharing platters for groups.
line: Old-school American barbecue on Hoxton Square: pulled pork, brisket, ribs and big sharing platters for groups.

name: The Princess of Shoreditch
why: A smart two-storey corner pub between Old Street and Hoxton, with a dining room upstairs and a popular Sunday roast.
line: A smart two-storey corner pub between Old Street and Hoxton, with a dining room upstairs and a popular Sunday roast.

name: The Wenlock Arms
why: A legendary real-ale pub on a quiet back street near the canal, saved by locals when it was threatened with closure. Changing guest ales and a proper old-fashioned welcome.
line: A legendary real-ale pub on a quiet back street near the canal, saved by locals when it was threatened with closure.

name: The George & Vulture
why: A big, friendly Hoxton pub on Pitfield Street with pizzas, pool and a relaxed crowd.
line: A big, friendly Hoxton pub on Pitfield Street with pizzas, pool and a relaxed crowd.

name: The Red Lion
why: A quirky, cosy Hoxton Street pub with mismatched furniture and a roof terrace up top. A good spot to start a night out.
line: A quirky, cosy Hoxton Street pub with mismatched furniture and a roof terrace up top.

name: Happiness Forgets
why: A small basement cocktail bar on Hoxton Square, often named one of the world's best bars. Brilliant drinks, no fuss, and fair prices. Book ahead.
line: A small basement cocktail bar on Hoxton Square, often named one of the world's best bars.

name: Colours Hoxton
why: An arts bar and club on Hoxton Square with live music, comedy and DJs, open from midday until late every day.
line: An arts bar and club on Hoxton Square with live music, comedy and DJs, open from midday until late every day.

name: Hoxton Street Market
why: Hackney's oldest street market, with street food, fruit and veg, and fashion and craft stalls on Saturdays. Pop into Hoxton Hall, a Victorian music hall, while you're there.
line: Hackney's oldest street market, with street food, fruit and veg, and fashion and craft stalls on Saturdays.

name: Hoxton Square
why: A leafy Georgian square at the heart of Hoxton, surrounded by bars, galleries and restaurants. Busy with people on the grass on summer evenings.
line: A leafy Georgian square at the heart of Hoxton, surrounded by bars, galleries and restaurants.

name: Kricket Brixton
why: Modern Indian small plates made with seasonal British produce, plus clever cocktails. It started life in a shipping container at Pop Brixton and grew into one of south London's favourites.
line: Modern Indian small plates made with seasonal British produce, plus clever cocktails.

name: Naughty Piglets
why: A small, much-loved bistro near Brockwell Park, open since 2015: a short menu that changes often, great natural wines and a warm welcome.
line: A small, much-loved bistro near Brockwell Park, open since 2015: a short menu that changes often, great natural wines and a warm welcome.

name: Wood & Water
why: Modern Jamaican cooking in Brixton, like duck with a jerk glaze, with rum cocktails and a buzzy room.
line: Modern Jamaican cooking in Brixton, like duck with a jerk glaze, with rum cocktails and a buzzy room.

name: The Begging Bowl
why: Regional Thai food in Peckham's Bellenden Road: charcoal-grilled dishes, fiery curries and unlimited jasmine rice. A local favourite for over a decade.
line: Regional Thai food in Peckham's Bellenden Road: charcoal-grilled dishes, fiery curries and unlimited jasmine rice.

name: Coal Rooms
why: A restaurant in Peckham Rye station's old Victorian ticket hall, cooking over coal and charcoal. The Sunday roast is a big cut above the usual.
line: A restaurant in Peckham Rye station's old Victorian ticket hall, cooking over coal and charcoal.

name: Brixton Village and Market Row
why: Covered market arcades in the heart of Brixton, packed with small restaurants and food stalls from all over the world: Caribbean, Colombian, Thai and much more. Brilliant for an evening of grazing.
line: Covered market arcades in the heart of Brixton, packed with small restaurants and food stalls from all over the world: Caribbean, Colombian, Thai and much more.

name: The Duke of Edinburgh
why: A Brixton pub with one of the biggest beer gardens in London, a pool table, craft beers and jerk chicken. Packed on sunny days.
line: A Brixton pub with one of the biggest beer gardens in London, a pool table, craft beers and jerk chicken.

name: The Effra
why: A Victorian Brixton pub with a grand old interior, live jazz and a bit of Caribbean cooking. A real local institution.
line: A Victorian Brixton pub with a grand old interior, live jazz and a bit of Caribbean cooking.

name: The Montpelier
why: A Peckham corner pub off Rye Lane with good food, a garden and a small cinema room in the back. Friendly and relaxed.
line: A Peckham corner pub off Rye Lane with good food, a garden and a small cinema room in the back.

name: The Camberwell Arms
why: A Camberwell gastropub between Brixton and Peckham, known for one of south London's best Sunday roasts, with big sharing cuts for two or three.
line: A Camberwell gastropub between Brixton and Peckham, known for one of south London's best Sunday roasts, with big sharing cuts for two or three.

name: Blues Kitchen Brixton
why: A bar and music venue with live blues, soul and rock'n'roll bands most nights, Cajun barbecue and a lively, late crowd.
line: A bar and music venue with live blues, soul and rock'n'roll bands most nights, Cajun barbecue and a lively, late crowd.

name: Peckham Levels
why: A multi-storey car park turned into a creative space, with bars, street food, studios and views over south London from the top floors.
line: A multi-storey car park turned into a creative space, with bars, street food, studios and views over south London from the top floors.

name: Peckham Cellars
why: A neighbourhood wine bar and restaurant with natural wines and a Basque-influenced menu. Easy for a glass or a full dinner.
line: A neighbourhood wine bar and restaurant with natural wines and a Basque-influenced menu.

name: Brockwell Park
why: A big, hilly park between Brixton and Herne Hill, with views of the City from the top, a walled garden, ponds and the famous 1930s lido at the bottom.
line: A big, hilly park between Brixton and Herne Hill, with views of the City from the top, a walled garden, ponds and the famous 1930s lido at the bottom.

name: Dosa n Chutney
why: South Indian favourites on Tooting High Street: crispy masala dosas, idly and vada thalis, all at very low prices. Book for dinner.
line: South Indian favourites on Tooting High Street: crispy masala dosas, idly and vada thalis, all at very low prices.

name: Apollo Banana Leaf
why: A Sri Lankan and South Indian café that has become a Tooting legend: mutton kothu roti, devilled dishes and fiery curries. Cheap, cheerful and bring your own drinks.
line: A Sri Lankan and South Indian café that has become a Tooting legend: mutton kothu roti, devilled dishes and fiery curries.

name: Lahore Karahi
why: A busy Pakistani grill by Tooting Broadway, open since 1995: sizzling karahis, grilled meats and samosa chaat.
line: A busy Pakistani grill by Tooting Broadway, open since 1995: sizzling karahis, grilled meats and samosa chaat.

name: Little Tapería
why: A small, cosy tapas bar with Spanish classics, cured meats and sangria. A good date-night spot.
line: A small, cosy tapas bar with Spanish classics, cured meats and sangria.

name: Daddy Bao
why: Fluffy Taiwanese bao and small plates on Mitcham Road, with a plum wine negroni to go with them.
line: Fluffy Taiwanese bao and small plates on Mitcham Road, with a plum wine negroni to go with them.

name: Tooting Market
why: A covered market running since the 1930s, now full of food stalls from Caribbean to Korean, alongside traditional traders. Its neighbour, Broadway Market, is next door.
line: A covered market running since the 1930s, now full of food stalls from Caribbean to Korean, alongside traditional traders.

name: The Wheatsheaf
why: A big, lively pub near Tooting Bec station with a back garden, pizzas, live sport and a popular Sunday roast.
line: A big, lively pub near Tooting Bec station with a back garden, pizzas, live sport and a popular Sunday roast.

name: The Selkirk
why: A dog-friendly, family-friendly backstreet pub with seasonal British food, a sunny beer garden and a Sunday roast with wine pairings.
line: A dog-friendly, family-friendly backstreet pub with seasonal British food, a sunny beer garden and a Sunday roast with wine pairings.

name: The Castle
why: Serving pints since 1832, with a heated garden full of little castle-shaped huts. A Sunday roast too.
line: Serving pints since 1832, with a heated garden full of little castle-shaped huts.

name: The Antelope
why: A grand Victorian pub with an open fire, homemade sausage rolls and local real ales. Cosy on a winter's evening.
line: A grand Victorian pub with an open fire, homemade sausage rolls and local real ales.

name: Goldfinch
why: A small, moody cocktail bar with very good negronis and a back garden.
line: A small, moody cocktail bar with very good negronis and a back garden.

name: Graveney & Meadow
why: An all-day café and bar by Tooting Broadway: coffee in the morning, cocktails at night, and a big garden with its own outdoor bar.
line: An all-day café and bar by Tooting Broadway: coffee in the morning, cocktails at night, and a big garden with its own outdoor bar.

name: Tooting Common
why: A big common with woods, a lake and Tooting Bec Lido, one of the largest open-air pools in the country (open all year, for the brave).
line: A big common with woods, a lake and Tooting Bec Lido, one of the largest open-air pools in the country (open all year, for the brave).

name: Artusi
why: A simple, whitewashed Italian on Bellenden Road with fresh pasta and a short menu that changes daily. Homely cooking at fair prices.
line: A simple, whitewashed Italian on Bellenden Road with fresh pasta and a short menu that changes daily.

name: Peckham Rye Park
why: Peckham Rye's park and common: a Japanese garden, a lake, woods and big open spaces, with cafés nearby on Lordship Lane. William Blake said he saw angels in a tree here as a boy.
line: Peckham Rye's park and common: a Japanese garden, a lake, woods and big open spaces, with cafés nearby on Lordship Lane.

name: Brunswick House
why: A grand Georgian mansion by Vauxhall Cross, now a restaurant crammed with chandeliers and antiques, all for sale. Chef Jackson Boxer's cooking is excellent, and there's jazz in the crypt bar. Great for a birthday.
line: A grand Georgian mansion by Vauxhall Cross, now a restaurant crammed with chandeliers and antiques, all for sale.

name: Daebak
why: A former greasy spoon turned Korean café: crispy Korean fried chicken in several sauces, stews and bibimbap, in big portions at low prices.
line: A former greasy spoon turned Korean café: crispy Korean fried chicken in several sauces, stews and bibimbap, in big portions at low prices.

name: Bonnington Café
why: A vegetarian and vegan café run by a co-operative of cooks since the 1980s, in a hidden corner by Bonnington Square. Each night a different cook, a different cuisine, and bring your own wine.
line: A vegetarian and vegan café run by a co-operative of cooks since the 1980s, in a hidden corner by Bonnington Square.

name: Adulis
why: An Eritrean restaurant near the Oval, serving big sharing platters of stews on injera bread. Lots for vegetarians. Dinner only.
line: An Eritrean restaurant near the Oval, serving big sharing platters of stews on injera bread.

name: The Black Dog
why: A friendly backstreet pub in Vauxhall with real ales, Spanish tapas and a traditional Sunday roast. It became a pilgrimage spot for Taylor Swift fans after she named a song after it.
line: A friendly backstreet pub in Vauxhall with real ales, Spanish tapas and a traditional Sunday roast.

name: The Prince of Wales
why: A traditional pub on Cleaver Square, one of the prettiest Georgian squares in south London. In summer, drinkers spill out onto the square for games of pétanque.
line: A traditional pub on Cleaver Square, one of the prettiest Georgian squares in south London.

name: The Black Prince
why: A Kennington local that starred in the film Kingsman: The Secret Service, where Colin Firth teaches the pub 'manners maketh man'. Friendly, with a big outdoor space.
line: A Kennington local that starred in the film Kingsman: The Secret Service, where Colin Firth teaches the pub 'manners maketh man'.

name: The Old Red Lion
why: A characterful Kennington pub with a mock-Tudor front, a beer garden and a good choice of ales. Handy for the Oval.
line: A characterful Kennington pub with a mock-Tudor front, a beer garden and a good choice of ales.

name: Royal Vauxhall Tavern
why: London's most famous LGBTQ+ venue, in a Victorian pub by Vauxhall Gardens. Cabaret, drag and club nights, and legend has it Freddie Mercury once smuggled Princess Diana in here in disguise.
line: London's most famous LGBTQ+ venue, in a Victorian pub by Vauxhall Gardens.

name: Vauxhall Food & Beer Garden
why: A busy outdoor bar and street-food yard tucked under the railway by Vauxhall station, with DJs at weekends.
line: A busy outdoor bar and street-food yard tucked under the railway by Vauxhall station, with DJs at weekends.

name: Kennington Park
why: A Victorian park on what was once Kennington Common, where huge Chartist crowds gathered in 1848. Today: a flower garden, a café, sports courts and playgrounds, close to the Oval.
line: A Victorian park on what was once Kennington Common, where huge Chartist crowds gathered in 1848.

name: Admiral Duncan
why: One of Soho's best-known gay pubs, on Old Compton Street, with resident drag queens and cabaret most nights. A memorial inside remembers those killed in the 1999 nail bomb attack.
line: One of Soho's best-known gay pubs, on Old Compton Street, with resident drag queens and cabaret most nights.

name: Comptons
why: One of London's oldest gay bars, a relaxed corner pub on Old Compton Street with live sport and DJs at weekends.
line: One of London's oldest gay bars, a relaxed corner pub on Old Compton Street with live sport and DJs at weekends.

name: She Soho
why: London's best-known lesbian bar, in a basement on Old Compton Street: comedy, cabaret, burlesque and DJs. Men are welcome only as guests of women or non-binary friends.
line: London's best-known lesbian bar, in a basement on Old Compton Street: comedy, cabaret, burlesque and DJs.

name: G-A-Y Bar
why: Three floors of pop videos, cheap drinks and DJs on Old Compton Street. Lively, loud and a classic start to a Soho night out.
line: Three floors of pop videos, cheap drinks and DJs on Old Compton Street.

name: The Duke of Wellington
why: A traditional two-storey Soho pub with a mainly gay crowd, live sport and quiz nights. Busy on the pavement outside on summer evenings.
line: A traditional two-storey Soho pub with a mainly gay crowd, live sport and quiz nights.

name: Rupert Street Bar
why: A stylish gay cocktail bar on Rupert Street with big windows, weekend DJs and drag cabaret.
line: A stylish gay cocktail bar on Rupert Street with big windows, weekend DJs and drag cabaret.

name: Village Soho
why: Often called Soho's first gay bar, with a relaxed, boudoir-style interior and happy hour deals. A good place for a quiet early drink.
line: Often called Soho's first gay bar, with a relaxed, boudoir-style interior and happy hour deals.

name: The Kings Arms
why: A friendly old Soho pub, popular with the bear community: real ales, karaoke, quizzes and drag bingo.
line: A friendly old Soho pub, popular with the bear community: real ales, karaoke, quizzes and drag bingo.

name: Ku Bar
why: One of London's biggest gay bars, on the edge of Chinatown, over three floors with a late-night club in the basement, open until 3am.
line: One of London's biggest gay bars, on the edge of Chinatown, over three floors with a late-night club in the basement, open until 3am.

name: Heaven
why: London's most famous gay club, in the arches under Charing Cross station since 1979. Home of the Saturday G-A-Y night, often with big pop stars and Drag Race queens on stage.
line: London's most famous gay club, in the arches under Charing Cross station since 1979.
address: The Arches, Villiers Street, London WC2N 6NG

name: Eagle London
why: An independent Vauxhall venue known for its Sunday Horse Meat Disco, one of London's best-loved club nights, plus drag and happy hours.
line: An independent Vauxhall venue known for its Sunday Horse Meat Disco, one of London's best-loved club nights, plus drag and happy hours.

name: The Cock Tavern
why: A Georgian Kennington pub turned queer bar, with DJs, burlesque, cabaret and drag, and dancing until 2am at weekends.
line: A Georgian Kennington pub turned queer bar, with DJs, burlesque, cabaret and drag, and dancing until 2am at weekends.

name: Two Brewers
why: South London's best-known gay bar, on Clapham High Street: cabaret on weeknights and drag club nights at weekends. Expect a queue on Saturdays.
line: South London's best-known gay bar, on Clapham High Street: cabaret on weeknights and drag club nights at weekends.

name: La Camionera
why: A friendly lesbian and queer bar in Hackney, run by and for women and non-binary people, with a small courtyard and regular event nights.
line: A friendly lesbian and queer bar in Hackney, run by and for women and non-binary people, with a small courtyard and regular event nights.

name: VQ Chelsea
why: The famous 24-hour café-bar on the Fulham Road (VQ is short for Vingt-Quatre, French for 24). Breakfast, burgers and a drink at any hour of the day or night. A Chelsea institution after a night out.
line: The famous 24-hour café-bar on the Fulham Road (VQ is short for Vingt-Quatre, French for 24).

name: VQ Bloomsbury
why: VQ's late-opening café-bar a few steps from the British Museum. Open late; the Fulham Road branch is the one that never closes, so check hours here before a late visit.
line: VQ's late-opening café-bar a few steps from the British Museum.

name: VQ Aldgate
why: VQ's late-opening café-bar in Aldgate, on the edge of the City and the East End. Open late; the Fulham Road branch is the one that never closes, so check hours here before a late visit.
line: VQ's late-opening café-bar in Aldgate, on the edge of the City and the East End.

name: Polo 24 Hour Bar
why: A no-frills 24-hour café and bar by Liverpool Street station, open round the clock since the 1950s. Full English breakfasts and a cold beer whenever you need them.
line: A no-frills 24-hour café and bar by Liverpool Street station, open round the clock since the 1950s.

name: Duck & Waffle
why: On the 40th floor of 110 Bishopsgate, with huge views over London, and famous for staying open around the clock. The signature duck and waffle at 4am is a London rite of passage. Check the hours before a very late visit. Thanksgiving 2026: a family-style feast of roasted bronze turkey and the trimmings on Thu 26 Nov, lunch 12pm–3pm (£65 a head) or dinner 5pm–10pm (£95).
line: On the 40th floor of 110 Bishopsgate, with huge views over London, and famous for staying open around the clock.

name: Heliot Steak House and Bar
why: The bar and restaurant inside the Hippodrome Casino on Leicester Square, open 24 hours. Cocktails and steaks overlooking the casino floor.
line: The bar and restaurant inside the Hippodrome Casino on Leicester Square, open 24 hours.
address: Hippodrome Casino, Cranbourn Street, London WC2H 7JH

name: Bar Italia
why: Soho's legendary Italian café-bar, open since 1949 and until 5am: espresso, a drink and people-watching under the neon sign. Ronnie Scott's is right opposite.
line: Soho's legendary Italian café-bar, open since 1949 and until 5am: espresso, a drink and people-watching under the neon sign.

name: Balans Soho No. 60
why: A Soho all-dayer on Old Compton Street, open until 5am midweek and 6am at weekends. Cocktails, comfort food and a boozy breakfast to finish the night.
line: A Soho all-dayer on Old Compton Street, open until 5am midweek and 6am at weekends.

name: Experimental Cocktail Club
why: A hidden cocktail bar behind an unmarked door in Chinatown, open until 3am, with excellent drinks and a buzzy late crowd.
line: A hidden cocktail bar behind an unmarked door in Chinatown, open until 3am, with excellent drinks and a buzzy late crowd.

name: Disrepute
why: A basement cocktail bar off Carnaby Street, in the old Kingly Club where the 1960s Profumo Affair began. Open until 3am most nights.
line: A basement cocktail bar off Carnaby Street, in the old Kingly Club where the 1960s Profumo Affair began.

name: Opium
why: A three-floor speakeasy in Chinatown with no sign outside, serving cocktails with dumplings until 3am at weekends.
line: A three-floor speakeasy in Chinatown with no sign outside, serving cocktails with dumplings until 3am at weekends.

name: The Lexington
why: A pub and music venue near Angel, with up-and-coming bands upstairs, a big American whiskey list, and open until 4am at weekends.
line: A pub and music venue near Angel, with up-and-coming bands upstairs, a big American whiskey list, and open until 4am at weekends.

name: Nightjar
why: A world-famous speakeasy by Old Street, regularly listed among the world's best bars: brilliant cocktails, live jazz and blues, open until 3am at weekends. Book ahead.
line: A world-famous speakeasy by Old Street, regularly listed among the world's best bars: brilliant cocktails, live jazz and blues, open until 3am at weekends.

name: Horse & Groom
why: A Shoreditch pub with a disco upstairs, open until 4am. Unpretentious and a lot of fun late on.
line: A Shoreditch pub with a disco upstairs, open until 4am.

name: The Ginger Pig, Marylebone
why: London's best-known butcher, with meat from its own farms on the North York Moors. The Marylebone shop is the original, with sausage rolls and pies to take away, and butchery classes.
line: London's best-known butcher, with meat from its own farms on the North York Moors.

name: The Ginger Pig, Clapham
why: The Ginger Pig's Abbeville Village shop: free-range meat from its own Yorkshire farms, plus pies, sausage rolls and ready-to-cook dishes.
line: The Ginger Pig's Abbeville Village shop: free-range meat from its own Yorkshire farms, plus pies, sausage rolls and ready-to-cook dishes.

name: The Ginger Pig, Hackney
why: The Ginger Pig by Victoria Park: rare-breed meat from its own farms, and good advice on what to cook.
line: The Ginger Pig by Victoria Park: rare-breed meat from its own farms, and good advice on what to cook.

name: The Ginger Pig, Borough Market
why: The Ginger Pig's stall inside Borough Market, with butchery classes. Pick up a joint, then the rest of dinner from the market around it.
line: The Ginger Pig's stall inside Borough Market, with butchery classes.

name: The Parson's Nose, Fulham
why: A family-run butcher near Parsons Green, with free-range British meat, game in season, a deli counter and ready meals. Also in Putney, South Kensington and Belgravia.
line: A family-run butcher near Parsons Green, with free-range British meat, game in season, a deli counter and ready meals.

name: The Parson's Nose, Putney
why: The Putney branch of the much-loved family butcher: free-range British meat, game in season and a deli counter, a short walk from the river.
line: The Putney branch of the much-loved family butcher: free-range British meat, game in season and a deli counter, a short walk from the river.

name: Turner & George
why: A Clerkenwell butcher for serious meat lovers: dry-aged beef, rare breeds and expert cuts, near Angel.
line: A Clerkenwell butcher for serious meat lovers: dry-aged beef, rare breeds and expert cuts, near Angel.

name: HG Walter
why: A family butcher in Barons Court, supplying many of London's top restaurants, with a shop counter open to all.
line: A family butcher in Barons Court, supplying many of London's top restaurants, with a shop counter open to all.

name: C. Lidgate
why: A family butcher in Holland Park since 1850, famous for its pies and organic meat.
line: A family butcher in Holland Park since 1850, famous for its pies and organic meat.

name: M. Moen & Sons
why: A traditional butcher on Clapham Common, with a lovely old shopfront, free-range meat, game and a deli.
line: A traditional butcher on Clapham Common, with a lovely old shopfront, free-range meat, game and a deli.

name: Hill & Szrok
why: A butcher on Broadway Market that turns into a restaurant in the evening, with steaks cooked on the marble counter.
line: A butcher on Broadway Market that turns into a restaurant in the evening, with steaks cooked on the marble counter.

name: William Rose
why: A friendly East Dulwich butcher with free-range meat and plenty of advice on how to cook it.
line: A friendly East Dulwich butcher with free-range meat and plenty of advice on how to cook it.

name: Godfrey's
why: A Highbury family butcher trading for generations, with free-range and organic meat and good sausages.
line: A Highbury family butcher trading for generations, with free-range and organic meat and good sausages.

name: Fin & Flounder
why: A family-run fishmonger on Broadway Market with day-boat fish, and lobster rolls and oysters from the counter at weekends.
line: A family-run fishmonger on Broadway Market with day-boat fish, and lobster rolls and oysters from the counter at weekends.

name: Moxon's, East Dulwich
why: One of London's best fishmongers, with fish straight from the coast and its own smokehouse. Also in Clapham South, Islington and South Kensington.
line: One of London's best fishmongers, with fish straight from the coast and its own smokehouse.

name: Moxon's, Clapham South
why: The original Moxon's fishmonger, by Clapham South station: day-boat fish, shellfish and its own smoked salmon.
line: The original Moxon's fishmonger, by Clapham South station: day-boat fish, shellfish and its own smoked salmon.
address: Westbury Parade, Nightingale Lane, London SW4 9DH

name: The Chelsea Fishmonger
why: A neighbourhood fishmonger off the King's Road, with fish picked daily and following the British seasons.
line: A neighbourhood fishmonger off the King's Road, with fish picked daily and following the British seasons.

name: The Sea, The Sea
why: A chef-run fish shop in Chelsea with dry-aged fish, and a seafood counter where you can eat in. Also in Hackney.
line: A chef-run fish shop in Chelsea with dry-aged fish, and a seafood counter where you can eat in.

name: Neal's Yard Dairy
why: The champion of British farmhouse cheese, in a little Covent Garden shop where they let you taste before you buy. Also at Borough Market.
line: The champion of British farmhouse cheese, in a little Covent Garden shop where they let you taste before you buy.

name: La Fromagerie
why: A beautiful cheese shop with a walk-in cheese room, a café and a deli, next door to The Ginger Pig. Also in Highbury and Bloomsbury.
line: A beautiful cheese shop with a walk-in cheese room, a café and a deli, next door to The Ginger Pig.

name: Paxton & Whitfield
why: One of London's oldest cheesemongers, trading since 1797 and holding a Royal Warrant. A must for a proper cheeseboard.
line: One of London's oldest cheesemongers, trading since 1797 and holding a Royal Warrant.

name: Mons Cheesemongers
why: A family cheesemonger at Borough Market known for raw-milk cheeses matured in its own cellars. Also in East Dulwich.
line: A family cheesemonger at Borough Market known for raw-milk cheeses matured in its own cellars.

name: Hamish Johnston
why: A Northcote Road cheese shop and deli with a big British and French range and friendly advice.
line: A Northcote Road cheese shop and deli with a big British and French range and friendly advice.

name: Rippon Cheese
why: A Pimlico cheese shop with hundreds of cheeses kept in a chilled shop. Wrap up warm.
line: A Pimlico cheese shop with hundreds of cheeses kept in a chilled shop.

name: Hedonism Wines
why: A spectacular Mayfair wine shop with thousands of bottles, from rare vintages to bottles under £30, and a self-service tasting machine.
line: A spectacular Mayfair wine shop with thousands of bottles, from rare vintages to bottles under £30, and a self-service tasting machine.

name: Philglas & Swiggot
why: An award-winning independent wine shop on Northcote Road, known for small producers and friendly advice.
line: An award-winning independent wine shop on Northcote Road, known for small producers and friendly advice.

name: Lea & Sandeman
why: A Fulham Road wine merchant strong on France, Italy and Spain, with helpful staff and good everyday bottles.
line: A Fulham Road wine merchant strong on France, Italy and Spain, with helpful staff and good everyday bottles.

name: Gerry's Wines & Spirits
why: A tiny Soho shop crammed with spirits from all over the world. If it exists, Gerry's probably stocks it.
line: A tiny Soho shop crammed with spirits from all over the world.

name: Milroy's of Soho
why: London's oldest whisky shop, with a secret bar hidden behind a bookcase downstairs.
line: London's oldest whisky shop, with a secret bar hidden behind a bookcase downstairs.

name: Uncorked
why: A City wine shop by Liverpool Street, strong on France, with fine wines and good advice.
line: A City wine shop by Liverpool Street, strong on France, with fine wines and good advice.

name: Theatre of Wine
why: An owner-run Greenwich wine shop full of characterful bottles from small producers.
line: An owner-run Greenwich wine shop full of characterful bottles from small producers.

name: E5 Bakehouse
why: A bakery and café in a railway arch by London Fields, milling its own flour for some of London's best sourdough.
line: A bakery and café in a railway arch by London Fields, milling its own flour for some of London's best sourdough.

name: Lina Stores
why: A Soho Italian deli since 1944, with a green-and-white shopfront, fresh pasta made daily, and cheeses and hams.
line: A Soho Italian deli since 1944, with a green-and-white shopfront, fresh pasta made daily, and cheeses and hams.

name: I. Camisa & Son
why: A tiny old Italian deli on Old Compton Street, packed with salami, cheeses and fresh pasta.
line: A tiny old Italian deli on Old Compton Street, packed with salami, cheeses and fresh pasta.

name: Gazzano's
why: A family Italian deli in Clerkenwell, once the heart of London's Little Italy.
line: A family Italian deli in Clerkenwell, once the heart of London's Little Italy.

name: Panzer's
why: A long-established St John's Wood deli and grocer, with smoked salmon, bagels and a huge range of food from around the world.
line: A long-established St John's Wood deli and grocer, with smoked salmon, bagels and a huge range of food from around the world.

name: Sally Clarke
why: The shop next to Sally Clarke's restaurant, with excellent bread, cakes, cheeses and ready-made dishes.
line: The shop next to Sally Clarke's restaurant, with excellent bread, cakes, cheeses and ready-made dishes.

name: Whole Foods Market, Kensington
why: A huge food store over three floors in the old Barkers department store, with organic produce, a cheese room, a bakery and places to eat.
line: A huge food store over three floors in the old Barkers department store, with organic produce, a cheese room, a bakery and places to eat.

name: M&S Marble Arch
why: Marks & Spencer's flagship, with a big food hall downstairs. Good for ready meals, sandwiches and a picnic.
line: Marks & Spencer's flagship, with a big food hall downstairs.

name: Granary Square
why: King's Cross's big square on the Regent's Canal, with over a thousand dancing fountain jets that children run through in summer, and wide steps down to the water. Coal Drops Yard, Dishoom and the Lightroom are all a few minutes' walk away.
line: King's Cross's big square on the Regent's Canal, with over a thousand dancing fountain jets that children run through in summer, and wide steps down to the water.

name: Gasholder Park
why: A small circular park built inside the restored iron frame of a Victorian gasholder, on the Regent's Canal. A peaceful spot for a sit-down.
line: A small circular park built inside the restored iron frame of a Victorian gasholder, on the Regent's Canal.

name: The Lighterman
why: A modern three-floor pub on Granary Square with terraces over the canal and good food: a Sunday roast (40-day-aged Dexter beef or half a Castlemead chicken) and, usually, fish and chips (Cornish hake).
line: A modern three-floor pub on Granary Square with terraces over the canal, a Sunday roast and fish and chips.

name: German Gymnasium
why: A grand restaurant in Britain's first purpose-built gym, built in the 1860s for the German Gymnastics Society, between King's Cross and St Pancras. Schnitzel, strudel and a big bar.
line: A grand restaurant in Britain's first purpose-built gym, built in the 1860s for the German Gymnastics Society, between King's Cross and St Pancras.

name: Word on the Water
why: A secondhand bookshop on an old Dutch barge moored by Granary Square, with live music on its roof on summer evenings.
line: A secondhand bookshop on an old Dutch barge moored by Granary Square, with live music on its roof on summer evenings.
address: Regent's Canal Towpath, Granary Square, London N1C 4AA

name: Everyman King's Cross
why: A comfy Everyman cinema by Pancras Square, with sofas, food and drinks brought to your seat. A good evening with dinner at Dishoom first.
line: A comfy Everyman cinema by Pancras Square, with sofas, food and drinks brought to your seat.

name: Prince Charles Cinema
why: London's favourite cult cinema, just off Leicester Square: cheap tickets, classic films, sing-along screenings and all-night film marathons.
line: London's favourite cult cinema, just off Leicester Square: cheap tickets, classic films, sing-along screenings and all-night film marathons.

name: Odeon Luxe Leicester Square
why: The cinema where the big film premieres happen, with red carpets on Leicester Square and reclining seats inside.
line: The cinema where the big film premieres happen, with red carpets on Leicester Square and reclining seats inside.

name: Curzon Soho
why: Soho's arthouse cinema, showing independent and foreign films, with a good bar.
line: Soho's arthouse cinema, showing independent and foreign films, with a good bar.

name: Picturehouse Central
why: A big, stylish cinema at Piccadilly Circus, with a members' bar and café. Handy before or after a West End dinner.
line: A big, stylish cinema at Piccadilly Circus, with a members' bar and café.
address: Corner of Shaftesbury Avenue and Great Windmill Street, London W1D 7DH

name: Regent Street Cinema
why: Called the birthplace of British cinema: the Lumière brothers showed moving pictures here in 1896, the first in Britain to a paying audience. Restored and showing films again.
line: Called the birthplace of British cinema: the Lumière brothers showed moving pictures here in 1896, the first in Britain to a paying audience.

name: BFI Southbank
why: The home of the British Film Institute, under Waterloo Bridge: classics, seasons and premieres, plus a free film archive you can browse.
line: The home of the British Film Institute, under Waterloo Bridge: classics, seasons and premieres, plus a free film archive you can browse.

name: BFI IMAX
why: One of the biggest cinema screens in the country, in the round building by Waterloo station. The place to see a blockbuster.
line: One of the biggest cinema screens in the country, in the round building by Waterloo station.

name: Barbican Cinema
why: The Barbican's cinemas show new releases, world cinema and film seasons, inside the famous concrete arts centre.
line: The Barbican's cinemas show new releases, world cinema and film seasons, inside the famous concrete arts centre.
address: Barbican Centre, Silk Street, London EC2Y 8DS

name: Electric Cinema, Portobello
why: One of Britain's oldest working cinemas, opened in 1911 on Portobello Road, with armchairs, footstools and beds in the front row.
line: One of Britain's oldest working cinemas, opened in 1911 on Portobello Road, with armchairs, footstools and beds in the front row.

name: Everyman Screen on the Green
why: A single-screen cinema on Islington Green with a famous red neon sign, showing films since 1913.
line: A single-screen cinema on Islington Green with a famous red neon sign, showing films since 1913.

name: Rio Cinema
why: Dalston's Art Deco community cinema, run as a charity, showing new releases, classics and festivals.
line: Dalston's Art Deco community cinema, run as a charity, showing new releases, classics and festivals.

name: The Castle Cinema
why: A Homerton cinema in a restored 1913 picture house, reopened in 2016 after a crowdfunding campaign, with a bar and cosy screens.
line: A Homerton cinema in a restored 1913 picture house, reopened in 2016 after a crowdfunding campaign, with a bar and cosy screens.

name: The Ritzy
why: Brixton's much-loved cinema since 1911, with a café-bar upstairs and live music some nights.
line: Brixton's much-loved cinema since 1911, with a café-bar upstairs and live music some nights.
address: Brixton Oval, Coldharbour Lane, London SW2 1JG

name: Genesis Cinema
why: An independent Whitechapel cinema with low ticket prices, a bar and some luxury screens.
line: An independent Whitechapel cinema with low ticket prices, a bar and some luxury screens.

name: Phoenix Cinema
why: One of the oldest cinemas in Britain still in use, in East Finchley since 1910, run by a charity.
line: One of the oldest cinemas in Britain still in use, in East Finchley since 1910, run by a charity.

name: Skuna Igloo Boats
why: Cosy see-through igloos on little electric boats at West India Quay, Canary Wharf, running all year in any weather. A short cruise round the dock, then cheese or chocolate fondue moored up. Each igloo takes 4 to 9 people, so it's great for a group. Book ahead, especially for Christmas.
line: Cosy see-through igloos on little electric boats at West India Quay, Canary Wharf, running all year in any weather.

name: Balloon Museum: Euphoria
why: A travelling exhibition of giant inflatable artworks at ExCeL's Waterfront, from late October 2026 until 22 August 2027: rooms of balloons and installations to touch, bounce and play in. Fun for all ages. Custom House station on the Elizabeth line is next door.
line: A travelling exhibition of giant inflatable artworks at ExCeL's Waterfront, from late October 2026 until 22 August 2027: rooms of balloons and installations to touch, bounce and play in.
address: ExCeL London Waterfront, Royal Victoria Dock, London E16 1XL

name: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory Afternoon Tea
why: A Roald Dahl afternoon tea at One Aldwych hotel: a roast dinner in sandwich form, a Violet Beauregarde dessert, hot chocolate and Wonka cocktails. A brilliant treat for children (and grown-ups) before a West End show. A festive version runs over Christmas.
line: A Roald Dahl afternoon tea at One Aldwych hotel: a roast dinner in sandwich form, a Violet Beauregarde dessert, hot chocolate and Wonka cocktails.

name: Absurd City
why: A huge, psychedelic immersive art world inside Westfield London in Shepherd's Bush, opened October 2026 by the team behind Bristol's Wake The Tiger and Boomtown festival. Four strange 'districts' to explore. Allow up to 2 hours.
line: A huge, psychedelic immersive art world inside Westfield London in Shepherd's Bush, opened October 2026 by the team behind Bristol's Wake The Tiger and Boomtown festival.
address: Westfield London, Ariel Way, London W12 7GF

name: Tokyo Bagel
why: A Japanese bagel café on Lower Marsh by Waterloo, with pink velvet armchairs and walls of roses, made for photos. Try a katsu chicken bagel or the honey toast.
line: A Japanese bagel café on Lower Marsh by Waterloo, with pink velvet armchairs and walls of roses, made for photos.
address: Unit B, 101 Lower Marsh, London SE1 7AB

name: The Double Helix Staircase, Fortnum & Mason
why: Fortnum's new double helix staircase: two staircases twisting round each other like DNA, from the lower ground to the second floor, inspired by Leonardo da Vinci. Hand-made with over 3,000 forged details and opened by the King in November 2025. Free to see while you shop.
line: Fortnum's new double helix staircase: two staircases twisting round each other like DNA, from the lower ground to the second floor, inspired by Leonardo da Vinci.

name: Chaos Karts
why: Real-life Mario Kart: electric go-karts on a projected track, where you collect power-ups and fire at your friends as you race. Under a railway arch near Brick Lane. Ages 13 and up.
line: Real-life Mario Kart: electric go-karts on a projected track, where you collect power-ups and fire at your friends as you race.

name: Wee Tiny Gallery
why: Possibly the smallest art gallery in the world: a brick-sized gallery at foot height under a shopfront on Brick Lane, near Princelet Street, with microscopic artworks inside. Look down or you'll walk straight past it.
line: Possibly the smallest art gallery in the world: a brick-sized gallery at foot height under a shopfront on Brick Lane, near Princelet Street, with microscopic artworks inside.

name: José
why: José Pizarro's tiny standing-room sherry and tapas bar on Bermondsey Street. Squeeze in for jamón, croquetas and a glass of fino. No bookings.
line: José Pizarro's tiny standing-room sherry and tapas bar on Bermondsey Street.

name: Pizarro
why: José Pizarro's bigger sit-down Spanish restaurant along the street from José: sharing plates, good Spanish wines and a relaxed buzz.
line: José Pizarro's bigger sit-down Spanish restaurant along the street from José: sharing plates, good Spanish wines and a relaxed buzz.

name: Casse-Croûte
why: A tiny, proper French bistro with a chalkboard menu that changes daily. Feels like a corner of Paris. Book ahead.
line: A tiny, proper French bistro with a chalkboard menu that changes daily.

name: Flour & Grape
why: Fresh pasta at fair prices, with a gin bar downstairs. A Bermondsey Street favourite, so expect a queue at weekends.
line: Fresh pasta at fair prices, with a gin bar downstairs.

name: The Woolpack
why: A friendly Victorian pub on Bermondsey Street with a beer garden out the back and a good Sunday roast.
line: A friendly Victorian pub on Bermondsey Street with a beer garden out the back and a good Sunday roast.

name: Bermondsey Beer Mile
why: A string of craft breweries and taprooms in the railway arches between London Bridge and South Bermondsey. Walk it on a Saturday, stopping for a half at each. Many open weekends only.
line: A string of craft breweries and taprooms in the railway arches between London Bridge and South Bermondsey.

name: Hide
why: A dark, stylish basement cocktail bar on Bermondsey Street, with seasonal drinks made with real care.
line: A dark, stylish basement cocktail bar on Bermondsey Street, with seasonal drinks made with real care.

name: Southwark Park
why: A big Victorian park with a boating lake, a bandstand, a café and a free art gallery. A peaceful break from the city.
line: A big Victorian park with a boating lake, a bandstand, a café and a free art gallery.

name: The Palmerston
why: A proper East Dulwich gastropub with wood panelling, seasonal British cooking and a much-loved Sunday roast.
line: A proper East Dulwich gastropub with wood panelling, seasonal British cooking and a much-loved Sunday roast.

name: Franklins
why: A neighbourhood restaurant on Lordship Lane, cooking hearty seasonal British food for over 20 years. Classic and reliable.
line: A neighbourhood restaurant on Lordship Lane, cooking hearty seasonal British food for over 20 years.

name: Toasted
why: A natural wine bar and restaurant with seasonal small plates, at the top of Lordship Lane. Good for a date.
line: A natural wine bar and restaurant with seasonal small plates, at the top of Lordship Lane.

name: The Crown & Greyhound
why: A huge, handsome Victorian pub in the middle of Dulwich Village, with a big garden. Popular with families for Sunday lunch.
line: A huge, handsome Victorian pub in the middle of Dulwich Village, with a big garden.

name: The Rosendale
why: A grand old West Dulwich pub with high ceilings, a big garden and a good choice of beers.
line: A grand old West Dulwich pub with high ceilings, a big garden and a good choice of beers.

name: The East Dulwich Tavern
why: The big corner pub at the bottom of Lordship Lane: live sport, quizzes and a busy, friendly crowd.
line: The big corner pub at the bottom of Lordship Lane: live sport, quizzes and a busy, friendly crowd.

name: Dulwich Park
why: A lovely Victorian park with a boating lake, a café, famous rhododendrons in spring and a playground. Across the road from the Dulwich Picture Gallery.
line: A lovely Victorian park with a boating lake, a café, famous rhododendrons in spring and a playground.

name: Marcella
why: A small, modern Italian on Deptford High Street with fresh pasta and a short menu that changes often. Fair prices for the quality.
line: A small, modern Italian on Deptford High Street with fresh pasta and a short menu that changes often.

name: Deptford Market Yard
why: A cobbled yard of restaurants, cafés and bars in the old railway arches by Deptford station, next to one of London's oldest railway lines.
line: A cobbled yard of restaurants, cafés and bars in the old railway arches by Deptford station, next to one of London's oldest railway lines.

name: Deptford Market
why: A proper south London street market on Deptford High Street: fruit and veg, bargains and bric-a-brac. Best on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays.
line: A proper south London street market on Deptford High Street: fruit and veg, bargains and bric-a-brac.

name: The Dog & Bell
why: A tucked-away backstreet pub with good real ales and a loyal crowd. An unspoilt London local.
line: A tucked-away backstreet pub with good real ales and a loyal crowd.

name: The Job Centre
why: A bar in Deptford's old job centre (yes, really), with DJs, cocktails and a fun, young crowd.
line: A bar in Deptford's old job centre (yes, really), with DJs, cocktails and a fun, young crowd.

name: The Albany
why: Deptford's arts centre, with theatre, comedy, gigs and children's shows, and a café.
line: Deptford's arts centre, with theatre, comedy, gigs and children's shows, and a café.

name: God's Own Junkyard
why: A warehouse packed with glowing neon signs, many made for films, from the late neon artist Chris Bracey. Free, dazzling and great for photos. Weekends only.
line: A warehouse packed with glowing neon signs, many made for films, from the late neon artist Chris Bracey.
address: Unit 12, Ravenswood Industrial Estate, Shernhall Street, London E17 9HQ

name: William Morris Gallery
why: The family home of the Victorian designer William Morris, now a free gallery of his wallpapers, fabrics and furniture, with a café and Lloyd Park behind.
line: The family home of the Victorian designer William Morris, now a free gallery of his wallpapers, fabrics and furniture, with a café and Lloyd Park behind.
address: Lloyd Park, Forest Road, London E17 4PP

name: Walthamstow Market
why: Said to be the longest daily street market in Europe, running about a kilometre down the High Street. Fruit, fabrics and everything else. Closed Mondays.
line: Said to be the longest daily street market in Europe, running about a kilometre down the High Street.

name: Eat17
why: A neighbourhood restaurant in pretty Walthamstow Village, famous locally for its 'bacon jam'. Good brunches and burgers.
line: A neighbourhood restaurant in pretty Walthamstow Village, famous locally for its 'bacon jam'.

name: The Nag's Head
why: A characterful village pub in Walthamstow Village, with a garden and a cosy, quirky interior.
line: A characterful village pub in Walthamstow Village, with a garden and a cosy, quirky interior.

name: The Bell
why: A big, busy corner pub by Walthamstow Central, with food, live sport and a Sunday roast.
line: A big, busy corner pub by Walthamstow Central, with food, live sport and a Sunday roast.

name: Wild Card Brewery
why: A Walthamstow craft brewery taproom on an industrial estate, part of the area's 'Blackhorse Beer Mile'. Lively at weekends.
line: A Walthamstow craft brewery taproom on an industrial estate, part of the area's 'Blackhorse Beer Mile'.

name: Lloyd Park
why: The park behind the William Morris Gallery, with a moat, a café, play areas and gardens.
line: The park behind the William Morris Gallery, with a moat, a café, play areas and gardens.

name: The Flask, Highgate
why: A historic village pub in Highgate with low beams, little rooms and a big front terrace. A perfect stop after the cemetery or Hampstead Heath.
line: A historic village pub in Highgate with low beams, little rooms and a big front terrace.

name: The Gatehouse
why: A big old pub on the site of Highgate's medieval tollgate, with a small theatre upstairs, Upstairs at the Gatehouse.
line: A big old pub on the site of Highgate's medieval tollgate, with a small theatre upstairs, Upstairs at the Gatehouse.

name: The Red Lion & Sun
why: A smart Highgate gastropub with a heated garden and a well-reviewed Sunday roast.
line: A smart Highgate gastropub with a heated garden and a well-reviewed Sunday roast.

name: Waterlow Park
why: A hillside park next to Highgate Cemetery with ponds, views over London and Lauderdale House, a Tudor house with a café.
line: A hillside park next to Highgate Cemetery with ponds, views over London and Lauderdale House, a Tudor house with a café.

name: Highgate Wood
why: Ancient woodland, once part of the old Forest of Middlesex, with a café and a big playground in the middle.
line: Ancient woodland, once part of the old Forest of Middlesex, with a café and a big playground in the middle.

name: Parkland Walk
why: A green walk along an old railway line from Finsbury Park towards Highgate, past old platforms. Look out for the 'spriggan' sculpture in an alcove at Crouch End.
line: A green walk along an old railway line from Finsbury Park towards Highgate, past old platforms.

name: Bistro Aix
why: A classic French bistro in Crouch End, serving steak frites, duck and crème brûlée. Romantic and good value.
line: A classic French bistro in Crouch End, serving steak frites, duck and crème brûlée.

name: Banners
why: A Crouch End institution with a colourful, laid-back room, famous for big breakfasts and a wide-ranging menu.
line: A Crouch End institution with a colourful, laid-back room, famous for big breakfasts and a wide-ranging menu.

name: The Harringay Arms
why: A small, traditional local in Crouch End: no music, no fuss, just good pints and conversation.
line: A small, traditional local in Crouch End: no music, no fuss, just good pints and conversation.

name: Crouch End Picturehouse
why: Crouch End's cinema, with a café-bar and a good mix of new releases and classics.
line: Crouch End's cinema, with a café-bar and a good mix of new releases and classics.

name: O2 Forum Kentish Town
why: A famous Art Deco gig venue that has hosted big names for decades. Kentish Town tube is next door.
line: A famous Art Deco gig venue that has hosted big names for decades.

name: Bull & Last
why: A top gastropub on the edge of Hampstead Heath, with excellent British cooking and a much-loved Sunday roast. Book ahead.
line: A top gastropub on the edge of Hampstead Heath, with excellent British cooking and a much-loved Sunday roast.

name: The Pineapple
why: A tucked-away Victorian backstreet pub in Kentish Town, saved from closure by its regulars. Proper local feel.
line: A tucked-away Victorian backstreet pub in Kentish Town, saved from closure by its regulars.

name: The Assembly House
why: A grand Victorian pub with etched glass and a big, high room, at the heart of Kentish Town.
line: A grand Victorian pub with etched glass and a big, high room, at the heart of Kentish Town.

name: The Engineer
why: A Primrose Hill gastropub with a lovely walled garden, named after Isambard Kingdom Brunel, who is said to have built it.
line: A Primrose Hill gastropub with a lovely walled garden, named after Isambard Kingdom Brunel, who is said to have built it.

name: The Princess of Wales
why: A friendly Primrose Hill local with a garden, a short walk from the hill itself.
line: A friendly Primrose Hill local with a garden, a short walk from the hill itself.

name: Lemonia
why: A big, bustling Greek taverna on Regent's Park Road, open for over 40 years and loved by locals: meze, grills and a warm welcome.
line: A big, bustling Greek taverna on Regent's Park Road, open for over 40 years and loved by locals: meze, grills and a warm welcome.

name: Parliament Hill
why: The south-east corner of Hampstead Heath, with one of London's best views across to St Paul's and the City. Protected by law, so nothing can block it.
line: The south-east corner of Hampstead Heath, with one of London's best views across to St Paul's and the City.

name: The Dove
why: A historic riverside pub on the Thames at Hammersmith, with a terrace over the water and what was once listed as the smallest bar room in Britain.
line: A historic riverside pub on the Thames at Hammersmith, with a terrace over the water and what was once listed as the smallest bar room in Britain.

name: The Blue Anchor
why: A cosy old riverside pub just by Hammersmith Bridge, with tables on the towpath. Great on Boat Race day.
line: A cosy old riverside pub just by Hammersmith Bridge, with tables on the towpath.

name: The Old Ship
why: A big riverside pub on the Thames path with a terrace and balcony, and a Sunday roast with a river view.
line: A big riverside pub on the Thames path with a terrace and balcony, and a Sunday roast with a river view.

name: The River Café
why: Ruth Rogers' famous Italian restaurant on the river, where many of today's top chefs trained. Michelin-starred, simple and expensive. Book well ahead.
line: Ruth Rogers' famous Italian restaurant on the river, where many of today's top chefs trained.
address: Thames Wharf, Rainville Road, London W6 9HA

name: Eventim Apollo
why: The big Art Deco venue at Hammersmith for gigs and stand-up comedy. Many of the UK's biggest comedians have filmed shows here.
line: The big Art Deco venue at Hammersmith for gigs and stand-up comedy.

name: Lyric Hammersmith
why: A theatre with a beautiful Victorian auditorium inside a modern building, known for bold productions and a big Christmas panto.
line: A theatre with a beautiful Victorian auditorium inside a modern building, known for bold productions and a big Christmas panto.
address: Lyric Square, King Street, London W6 0QL

name: O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire
why: An old variety theatre, once BBC TV studios, now one of London's best mid-sized gig venues.
line: An old variety theatre, once BBC TV studios, now one of London's best mid-sized gig venues.

name: Shepherd's Bush Market
why: A lively street market under the railway with food, fabrics and stalls from all over the world. Closed Sundays.
line: A lively street market under the railway with food, fabrics and stalls from all over the world.

name: Bush Theatre
why: A small theatre in an old library on Shepherd's Bush Green, known for new writing, with a good café-bar.
line: A small theatre in an old library on Shepherd's Bush Green, known for new writing, with a good café-bar.

name: Ravenscourt Park
why: A friendly park with a pond, tennis courts, a café and play areas, between Hammersmith and Chiswick.
line: A friendly park with a pond, tennis courts, a café and play areas, between Hammersmith and Chiswick.

name: The City Barge
why: A riverside pub on pretty Strand-on-the-Green, with a Sunday roast. It appeared in the Beatles film Help!
line: A riverside pub on pretty Strand-on-the-Green, with a Sunday roast.

name: The Bull's Head
why: An old riverside pub on Strand-on-the-Green, with tables by the water. Watch the tide: the path floods at very high tides.
line: An old riverside pub on Strand-on-the-Green, with tables by the water.

name: Bell & Crown
why: A Fuller's pub on the river at Strand-on-the-Green, with a conservatory looking over the Thames.
line: A Fuller's pub on the river at Strand-on-the-Green, with a conservatory looking over the Thames.

name: La Trompette
why: A Michelin-starred neighbourhood French restaurant just off Chiswick High Road. Polished cooking, without the West End prices.
line: A Michelin-starred neighbourhood French restaurant just off Chiswick High Road.

name: The Swan, Chiswick
why: A backstreet gastropub with a lovely garden and a good Sunday roast.
line: A backstreet gastropub with a lovely garden and a good Sunday roast.
address: 1 Evershed Walk, 119 Acton Lane, London W4 5HH

name: Fuller's Griffin Brewery
why: Beer has been brewed on this Chiswick site since the 1600s, home of London Pride. Brewery tours and a shop. Check tour times before you go.
line: Beer has been brewed on this Chiswick site since the 1600s, home of London Pride.

name: Hogarth's House
why: The country home of the 18th-century painter William Hogarth, now a small free museum of his prints.
line: The country home of the 18th-century painter William Hogarth, now a small free museum of his prints.
address: Hogarth Lane, Great West Road, London W4 2QN

name: The White Cross
why: Richmond's famous riverside pub, right on the Thames. At very high tides the river floods the path, and drinkers have to use the side door.
line: Richmond's famous riverside pub, right on the Thames.

name: The Roebuck
why: A pub at the top of Richmond Hill, with the famous view over the Thames bend across the road. Take your drink out on to the terrace.
line: A pub at the top of Richmond Hill, with the famous view over the Thames bend across the road.

name: The Prince's Head
why: A traditional pub on Richmond Green that plays the Crown & Anchor in Ted Lasso, with the famous bench outside. Fans come from all over the world. The Official Ted Lasso Store is a few doors away on Paved Court.
line: A traditional pub on Richmond Green that played the Crown & Anchor in Ted Lasso.

name: Petersham Nurseries Café
why: Lunch in a beautiful greenhouse full of plants, on the edge of Petersham Meadows. Seasonal Italian-leaning cooking. Book ahead.
line: Lunch in a beautiful greenhouse full of plants, on the edge of Petersham Meadows.
address: Church Lane, Petersham Road, Richmond TW10 7AB

name: Richmond Hill view
why: The view over the bend of the Thames from Richmond Hill, painted by Turner and Reynolds. It's the only view in England protected by an Act of Parliament.
line: The view over the bend of the Thames from Richmond Hill, painted by Turner and Reynolds.

name: Ham House
why: A remarkable 17th-century house by the Thames, run by the National Trust and said to be one of the most haunted in Britain. Lovely gardens.
line: A remarkable 17th-century house by the Thames, run by the National Trust and said to be one of the most haunted in Britain.

name: Richmond Theatre
why: A beautiful Victorian theatre on Richmond Green, with touring shows and a big Christmas panto. Rebecca's charity gala in Ted Lasso was filmed here.
line: A beautiful Victorian theatre on Richmond Green, with touring shows and a big Christmas panto.

name: The Florence
why: A big, friendly pub by Brockwell Park in Herne Hill, with a garden, a Sunday roast and room for families. A short walk from Brixton.
line: A big, friendly pub by Brockwell Park in Herne Hill, with a garden, a Sunday roast and room for families.

name: The Victoria, East Sheen
why: A smart gastropub near the Sheen Gate of Richmond Park, with a garden and a well-liked Sunday roast. Perfect after a walk in the park.
line: A smart gastropub near the Sheen Gate of Richmond Park, with a garden and a well-liked Sunday roast.

name: British Library
why: The national library, with a free Treasures gallery: Magna Carta, Shakespeare's First Folio, Beatles lyrics in their own handwriting and Leonardo's notebooks.
line: The national library, with a free Treasures gallery: Magna Carta, Shakespeare's First Folio, Beatles lyrics in their own handwriting and Leonardo's notebooks.

name: St Pancras International
why: One of the world's most beautiful stations, home of the Eurostar. Look up at the great Victorian roof, then find the giant 'Meeting Place' lovers and the statue of John Betjeman, who saved it from demolition.
line: One of the world's most beautiful stations, home of the Eurostar.

name: Christ Church Spitalfields
why: Nicholas Hawksmoor's towering 1720s church, opposite Spitalfields Market. Light, white and grand inside.
line: Nicholas Hawksmoor's towering 1720s church, opposite Spitalfields Market.

name: The Ten Bells
why: A Victorian pub opposite Christ Church, linked to Jack the Ripper: two of his victims are said to have drunk here. Original tiles inside.
line: A Victorian pub opposite Christ Church, linked to Jack the Ripper: two of his victims are said to have drunk here.

name: Boxpark Shoreditch
why: A pop-up mall built from shipping containers by Shoreditch High Street station, with street food and bars upstairs.
line: A pop-up mall built from shipping containers by Shoreditch High Street station, with street food and bars upstairs.

name: Keats House
why: The Hampstead house where John Keats lived and fell in love, and wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale', it's said under a plum tree in the garden.
line: The Hampstead house where John Keats lived and fell in love, and wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale', it's said under a plum tree in the garden.

name: The Official Ted Lasso Store
why: The official AFC Richmond shop, over two floors on Paved Court, a few doors from Ted's flat and the Crown & Anchor: kits, scarves, hats and 'Believe' signs. Opened in 2024; check opening times before a special trip.
line: The official AFC Richmond shop, over two floors on Paved Court, a few doors from Ted's flat and the Crown & Anchor: kits, scarves, hats and 'Believe' signs.

name: Paved Court (Ted's street)
why: The narrow lane of little shops off Richmond Green where Ted Lasso lives in the show, right next to the pub. Fans come from all over the world for photos.
line: The narrow lane of little shops off Richmond Green where Ted Lasso lives in the show, right next to the pub.

name: Richmond Bridge
why: London's oldest surviving Thames bridge, from the 1770s, with lovely views up and down the river. The riverside here appears in Ted Lasso, and the boats leave from just below.
line: London's oldest surviving Thames bridge, from the 1770s, with lovely views up and down the river.

name: Selhurst Park
why: Crystal Palace's home ground, which plays AFC Richmond's 'Nelson Road' stadium in Ted Lasso. Catch a Palace match for a real south London football atmosphere.
line: Crystal Palace's home ground, which plays AFC Richmond's 'Nelson Road' stadium in Ted Lasso.

name: Bermondsey Bierkeller
why: Oktoberfest under the arches, all year round. A huge Bavarian beer hall in the old London Bridge vaults, with steins, bratwurst, schnitzel and pretzels, live sport on the big screens, and a vault full of games from shuffleboard to drift karting. Great for groups – stag dos, birthdays and office parties – and a few minutes from Borough Market. Its own Oktoberfest runs every September into October. Open every day from noon, until 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.
line: Oktoberfest under the arches, all year round.
story: These are the arches that carried the approach to the old London Bridge, and the London Bridge Experience next door is run by the same people. Got a Go City pass? It includes a meal here.

name: Museum Tavern
why: A Victorian pub right opposite the British Museum, with etched glass, dark wood and proper ales. The obvious place to rest your feet after the museum.
line: A Victorian pub right opposite the British Museum, with etched glass, dark wood and proper ales.
story: Karl Marx is said to have drunk here while he was writing in the British Museum's Reading Room across the road.

name: Sicilian Avenue
why: A little Edwardian pedestrian street from 1910, with Italian-style columns at each end and café tables outside. A quiet short cut between Southampton Row and Bloomsbury Way.
line: A little Edwardian pedestrian street from 1910, with Italian-style columns at each end and café tables outside.
story: Built to look like a street in Italy – it's one of the few pedestrian shopping streets of its age left in London.

name: Gordon Ramsay Hell's Kitchen
why: The TV show turned restaurant, and the first one in the UK, in The Cumberland at Marble Arch. Red and blue kitchens, beef Wellington, lobster risotto and a five-course tasting menu, with DJs during the week. Big, loud and fun for groups – there are four chef's tables to book.
line: The TV show turned restaurant, and the first one in the UK, in The Cumberland at Marble Arch.
story: Marble Arch is where the Tyburn gallows stood for around 600 years – look for the stone set in the road at the top of Edgware Road. Hyde Park and Speakers' Corner are across the road, Selfridges a short walk down Oxford Street.
address: The Cumberland, Great Cumberland Place, London W1H 7DL

name: Regency Café
